root_cause.text: The cleanup loop uses `while(i--)` which decrements `i` before processing, causing the element at the current failing index to be skipped and not freed when the initialization loop jumps to the cleanup label on failure.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the loop from `while(i--)` to `do { ... } while(i--)`, ensuring that the cleanup code executes at least once for the current index `i` before decrementing. In the original code, when a failure occurs at index `i`, the `while(i--)` condition immediately decrements `i` to `i-1` before the first iteration, skipping the cleanup of the device at the failing index and causing a memory leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one error in NIC device cleanup loop to ensure all allocated devices are properly destroyed during setup failure.
intent_record.what: Changed the error cleanup loop from a while(i--) pre-decrement loop to a do-while(i--) post-decrement loop structure.
intent_record.how: This ensures the cleanup code executes at least once even if i=0 initially, and processes all devices from the current index down to 0 inclusive. The do-while guarantees the loop body runs before the condition is checked, whereas the original while loop could skip execution if i started at 0.

grouping_result.intent: Fix off-by-one error in NIC device cleanup loop to ensure all allocated devices are properly destroyed during setup failure.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by fixing the off-by-one error in the cleanup loop. The vulnerability describes how `while(i--)` skips the element at the current failing index, and this group's intent is to fix exactly that issue to ensure all allocated devices are properly freed during setup failure.

candidates.rationale: The pre-decrement in the while condition causes i to be decremented before the loop body executes. When the initialization loop fails at index i and jumps to cleanup, the while(i--) skips processing the element at the current failing index because i is decremented first, leaving that device unfreed. The fix should use while(i--) with proper initialization or change to while(--i) or similar to ensure the failing index is included in cleanup.

vuln_statements.explanation: The post-decrement operator in the while condition causes i to be decremented before the loop body executes. When the initialization loop fails at index i and jumps to the cleanup label, this while(i--) skips processing the element at the current failing index because the decrement happens first, leaving that device unfreed. This is an off-by-one error in the cleanup loop that fails to properly destroy all allocated NIC devices during setup failure.
